findings.defect: The two halves of thm:mono-iff do not compose, and the missing step is never stated. (a) yields a readout system that need be neither DYADIC nor delta-LEAKY; (b) requires both. GAP (one sentence): every readout system of order (m,r) realising s can be replaced by a dyadic delta-leaky readout system of order (m,r) realising the same s. Without it (i) the headline "realisability ... is EQUIVALENT to a concave interpolation problem" is not proved, (ii) prop:mono-gsharp's closing sentence applies thm:mono-iff(b) to a system that fails its hypothesis, and (iii) lem:mono-perturb -- the engine of thm:mono-kbound, the route's only new lower bound -- perturbs the INTERCEPTS only and then asserts "picking a dyadic eta there and applying thm:mono-iff(b) produces H'", which is unavailable whenever the gradients p and intercepts q of H are not themselves dyadic. They generically are not: lem:denominator-sharp gives denominators dividing an integer <= 2^a, not a power of two.
findings.evidence: I recomputed G#'s eight readouts exactly from /tmp/.../monotone-lemma/ap_h7_game.json by pinning the Max vertices and eliminating each vertex's own value (readouts.py): three of the eleven distinct pieces are NOT dyadic -- (0,0) has const 4/121 with coefficients {1: 29/704, 2: 87/121, 3: 1/121} and const 65/1936 with {1: 3/121, 2: 2845/3872, 3: 1/121}, and (1,1) has const 55/124. These pieces are exactly the affine readouts of the one-player games G#_tau that lem:mono-perturb is applied to inside thm:mono-kbound, so the asserted final step of that lemma has a concrete instance where its hypothesis fails. B^2's realising game likewise has non-dyadic readouts. (The repair is a five-line density argument -- shrink all rows by 1-eps, round to dyadics, strictness is open -- but it is asserted, not proved.)

findings.defect: rem:mono-proj (and the closing sentence of the prop:mono-proj result entry) drops prop:mono-proj's hypothesis and asserts "every improvement orientation of a NONDEGENERATE stopping SSG is the sink projection of a unique sink orientation of the (m+k)-cube". prop:mono-proj assumes the strictly stronger "no profile (sigma,tau) ties any controlled vertex's two successors"; def:improvement-uso's nondegeneracy only forbids ties in val_sigma at MAX vertices. Under the reading prop:mono-proj supplies (the profile orientation), the general statement is false.
findings.evidence: Explicit counterexample, verified exactly with my own core: kinds ['max','min','avg','avg','avg'], succ [[2,4],[2,3],[t1,t0],[t0,t1],[t0,3]] with t0=5, t1=6 (all successor pairs distinct). Stopping True; improvement outmap (0,1) with NO tied Max incidence, so the game is nondegenerate. But val(2) = val(3) = 1/2 under all four profiles, so the Min coordinate is tied at every profile: the profile 2-cube has no out-edge in the Min direction at either end of its Min edges, hence two sinks on a 1-face, hence is not a USO.

findings.defect: The final inference is a non sequitur. From "more than c*2^m/m^4 pieces in some readout" and thm:mono-iff(a) one gets k > m - 4log2 m - O(1) MIN VERTICES, which bounds the vertex count below by Omega(m), not by 2^{Omega(m)}. The clause "and so 2^{Omega(m)} vertices" does not follow from anything in the route; it follows from prop:auso-size (at most 2^{O(N log N)} orientations from games on <= N vertices), which is the paper's, not the route's, and is precisely what rem:mono-count claims to be improving on. Two smaller slips in the same proof: the polynomial count is r^{m+1} m 2^m rather than r^m m 2^m (the sign conditions range over the pieces of the OTHER action too), and Warren's bound needs the observation that each realised outmap is attained at a parameter point where no auxiliary polynomial vanishes (true by openness, unstated). Neither affects the exponent O(r m^3 log 2r), which I checked.
findings.evidence: n = 2rm^2, D = O(m), M = r^{m+1} m 2^m gives n log(4eDM/n) = O(r m^3 log 2r), so the counting half is right; A(3) = 728 (my enumeration) and A(m) >= A(m-1)^2 give 728^{2^{m-3}} > 2^{1.18*2^m} (log2 728 / 8 = 1.1885), and A(4) = 4792176 >= 728^2 = 529984 confirms the recursion numerically.

findings.defect: The "708 incidences / 708 improving switches over 34 explicit games" measurement is dominated by instances on which both laws are vacuous or already known. Only 3 of the 34 games have Min vertices, contributing 112 of the 1416 incidences, i.e. 56 of the 708 switches and 56 of the 708 hull tests. On a one-player game Psi is affine, so prop:mono-hull is automatic (x_sigma is not even in the AFFINE hull of the opposite face), and prop:mono-switchmax is strictly weaker than thm:impedance, which gives d(v) = d(u) h(v->u) <= d(u). verdict:
NOT SOUND as submitted: two major findings survive, though nothing is fatal and every single computational claim reproduced exactly.

The mathematics is largely correct and the exact-arithmetic work is of high quality. I rebuilt all of it independently -- the 3-cube census (728/18/16/656), the completeness of the 12640-class 4-cube census (my own C enumerator counts 4792176 AUSOs), the 182 translate-carrying classes with their height x Holt-Klee split, chi_HK for the height-7 orientation and for all ten 4-faces of B^2, B^2's face and translate statistics, G#'s eight readouts, all 34 explicit games from their raw adjacency lists, and both new laws (708/708, 708/708) -- and found no discrepancy anywhere.

The two major defects are:

(1) The route's central open question is closed, and closed in its own currency. frontier.tex now contains prop:b2-realised: B^2 is the improvement outmap of a nondegenerate stopping SSG on 138 vertices with five Max and ONE Min vertex. I verified that game from scratch and then extracted its readout system: order exactly (5,2). That is a direct affirmative answer to rem:mono-gap's "sharp missing statement for the pivot", and it makes the headline ("tested at the smallest open size"), the B^2 result line, and next_steps item 1 stale. It also shows thm:mono-kbound's k >= 1 for B^2 is tight, which strengthens the route's own bound.

(2) thm:mono-iff's halves do not compose. Direction (a) produces a readout system that need be neither dyadic nor delta-leaky; direction (b) requires both. The missing density/rounding lemma is never stated, and it is not decorative: lem:mono-perturb -- the engine of thm:mono-kbound, the route's only new lower bound -- ends by "picking a dyadic eta ... and applying thm:mono-iff(b)" to a system whose gradients and intercepts are in general not dyadic, and I exhibited the concrete instances (G#'s frozen one-player games have readout denominators 121, 124, 1936). The same gap makes prop:mono-gsharp's closing sentence an application of thm:mono-iff(b) to a system that fails its hypothesis. The repair is short but it is asserted, not proved.

Beyond those: rem:mono-proj asserts prop:mono-proj without its hypothesis and is false as stated (I give a seven-vertex nondegenerate stopping SSG whose profile cube is not a USO); lem:subgame and thm:opt-subcube are cited for statements they do not make, and thm:contraction/thm:lfp-general are applied to the many-sink game G[y] outside the setting they are stated for; prop:mono-count's "and so 2^{Omega(m)} vertices" does not follow from its own premises (it is prop:auso-size's conclusion); "twelve Min vertices" should be eight; the m = 4 coverage numbers are numpy floats presented as facts; and rem:mono-translate's novelty contrast is contradicted by the corrected text of rem:blowup-realise, which already records a single-coordinate translated layer realised by a one-player game.

What genuinely stands, and is verified: prop:mono-m3 in full (all 18 classes of the 3-cube realised, one-player exactly on the 16 Holt-Klee ones, sizes and denominators as claimed); the readout theorem and lem:mono-reduce; prop:mono-hull and prop:mono-switchmax (though only 56 of the 708 tests are on games where either says anything a one-player theorem does not already say); prop:mono-gsharp apart from its last sentence; thm:mono-kbound modulo the rounding gap; and, as the route's real new datum, thirteen exactly verified one-player games at m = 4 that translate a whole 3-cube between parallel facets.
